meetings.title: 13th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee continued its work regarding the Bill on the ... Amendment to Act No. 2010/7 (Decentralization Act). As a first item, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to extend the deadline of the Bill until 24th August 2026. This was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed unanimously by the members present and participating in the vote. Afterwards, while the administrative desk was reading the Bill, Kendhoo Constituency Member Mauroof Zakir took the floor and proposed to proceed with the work on this Bill after taking into consideration the decision of the Petition Committee regarding the petitions submitted to that committee in relation to this Bill. This was seconded by Keyodhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Niushad. When put to a vote, this proposal failed to pass by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Subsequently, Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz proposed to proceed with the work on the Bill as agendized. This was seconded by Vilifushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Afterwards, after the administrative desk read the Bill, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to remove from the Bill the amendment proposed under Article 1 of the Bill to add a clause after Section 56-2 (l) of the said Act. This was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Furthermore, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to add an article as Article 1 of the Bill to amend Section 56-2 (c) of the Act. This was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan also proposed to add an article as Article 2 of the Bill to amend Section 56-2 (d) of the Act. This was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Moreover, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to add an article as Article 3 of the Bill to amend Section 65 (b) (1) of the Act. This was seconded by Naifaru Constituency Member Yasin Abdulla. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. After that, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to pass the article proposed as Article 4 of the Bill to add a clause after Section 107-2 (d) of the Act as proposed. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Next, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to pass the article proposed as Article 5 of the Bill to add a clause after Section 131-1 (k) of the Act as proposed. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed unanimously by the members present and participating in the vote. Then, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to pass the article proposed as Article 5 of the Bill to add a clause after Section 131-2 (e) of the Act as proposed. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Afterwards, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to add an article as Article 7 of the Bill. This was seconded by Naifaru Constituency Member Yasin Abdulla. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. After that, Henveiru Uthuru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to pass the article proposed as Article 8 of the Bill as proposed. When put to a vote, this proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Finally, discussions were held regarding the petitions submitted to the Petition Committee, taking into consideration the number of signatures from the public on those petitions and the matters highlighted in the petitions.

meetings.title: 9th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: The work carried out at today’s meeting was to review the matters submitted to the committee. First, regarding the matter that was submitted concerning the illegal allocation of a large plot of land in the Addu City Meedhoo Tourism Zone to a private party without a bidding process, Henveiru North Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to administratively check the progress of this investigation and to continue working on the issue once information is received. It was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. When the proposal was put to a vote, it was passed unanimously by the members present and participating in the committee vote. After that, the committee reviewed two issues regarding the Addu City Council. The first was a request to investigate a decision made by the Land Committee, which includes Mayor Ali Nizar. The committee had decided to waive off 10 years of unpaid rent and fines for a fishing plot leased in 2013 to a company registered to the Mayor’s brother, and to extend the lease to 20 years. The second issue involved a private company that failed to supply three road sweepers. Instead of enforcing the contract's penalties, the council unlawfully canceled the agreement and forgave the advance payment and damages owed by the company. Henveiru North Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to check the progress of the investigations into both matters and to proceed with further work once more information is received. It was seconded by Nilandhoo Constituency Member Fathimath Saudha. When the proposal was put to a vote, it was unanimously approved by the members present and participating in the committee vote. Next, the committee proceeded to discuss a letter requesting an update on the committee's actions regarding the resolution ‘Nurturing hope, securing peace and ensuring justice for future generations,’ which was passed at the 152nd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union in Istanbul. Henveiru North Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to administratively gather the requested information and prepare a response to submit to the committee. This was seconded by Addu Meedhoo Constituency Member Abdul Rahman. When the proposal was put to a vote, it was unanimously approved by the members present and participating in the committee vote.

meetings.title: 7th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the Committee first addressed the issue submitted by the Male' City Council regarding the Ministry of National Planning, Housing & Infrastructure, informing the Council of the termination of the Male' Streetscaping project on 23 June 2023. When queried by the Committee on whether the Council still wished to pursue a review of this matter, the Male' City Council responded that they no longer seek further review. Due to this North Henveyru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to file the issue and this was seconded by Naifaru Constituency Member Yaaseen Abdulla. The Committee unanimously passed the motion. The second issue the Committee reviewed was the issue submitted by R. Innamaadhoo Council requesting to amend the Regulation number: 6-2018 (s.11). It was noted that the relevant Ministry had already informed the Council that they are working on the issue. Therefore, North Henveyru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan proposed to file the issue and Keyodhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Niushad seconded the motion. The Committee unanimously passed the motion. The third issue that the Committee reviewed was the issue submitted by Sh. Funadhoo Council regarding the Ministry of Finance’s direction to register the land on which Funadhoo Airport has been developed in the name of the Ministry of Finance. Keyodhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Niushad proposed to request an update on the issue before the Committee proceeds and this was seconded by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. The Committee unanimously passed the motion. The fourth issue the Committee reviewed was the Local Government Authority’s issue concerning the management and maintenance of record of the work visas issued to expatriate workers under the Decentralization Act. Since this issue is submitted to the Ministry of Homeland Security and Technology, Kolamaafushi Constituency Member Ibrahim Didi proposed to file the issue and Keyodhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Niushad seconded the motion. The Committee unanimously passed the motion. The fifth issue the Committee reviewed was the issue forwarded by the Public Accounts Committee regarding the matter raised by the Thinadhoo Council, seeking clarification on the classifications of elective positions of Mayors, Presidents of Atoll Councils, Presidents of Island Councils and Council members governed by Law number 7/2010 (Decentralization Act). Thinadhoo Council mentioned despite these positions being under the purview of the People's Majlis for remuneration decisions, the categorization of these roles needs to be clarified. Consequently, various state institutions treat them differently, leading to challenges in accessing state-provided services. Following extensive deliberation on the information provided by the Authorities regarding the issue, Vilifushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed proposed to respond to Thinadhoo Council stating the Committee would address the issue when further amendments are brought to the Law number 7/2010 (Decentralization Act). This proposal was seconded by North Henveyru Constituency Member Ahmed Aifan. The Committee unanimously passed the motion. The last issue that the Committee reviewed was the issue referred to the Committee by the Government Oversight Committee concerning a submission from the Faadhippolhu Atoll Council regarding the Atoll’s State House. The Council highlighted that the anticipated repair costs for the State House building exceed those for constructing a new building. Consequently, they have requested either the construction of a new building or a solution to transfer ownership of the State House building to the Council. The Committee reviewed the information sent from the Ministry of Cities, Local Government, and Public Works, which noted that the PSIP (2025) includes a new building for the Faadhippolhu Atoll State House. Kolamaafushi Constituency Member Ibrahim Didi proposed that this information be communicated to the Faadhippolhu Atoll Council and that the matter be considered closed. This proposal was seconded by Vilufushi Constituency Member Hassan Waheed. T he Committee unanimously passed the motion.
